Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 42, verse 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Shura (Consultation), because the believers are described in it as consulting one another in their affairs, and this quality is among the praiseworthy virtues and noble traits that deserve to be pointed out and commended.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Establishing the source of revelation and the unity of the foundations of religion from the earliest prophethoods to the final message, and explaining God's choosing of the seal of His prophets, upon him and them be blessings and peace; by sending down the Qur'an to him, and prescribing for him of religion what He enjoined upon the prophets before him, so that he may warn all creatures.

• Severe warning to the opponents who dispute with falsehood, and admonition to those who deny the Qur'an and deny the Resurrection, and mention of what the polytheists will meet of punishment on the Day of Reckoning, and what the believers will meet of honour.

• Rebuke of the polytheists for attributing fabrication to the Prophet (ﷺ), and consolation of the Messenger (ﷺ) that God is the one who will take care of their recompense.

• Mention of the proofs of God's oneness and the signs of divine power in the creation of this universe, reminder of God's blessings, warning against causing their loss through evil deeds, urging the pursuit of the means of success in the Hereafter, and hastening to do so before it is too late.

• Noting a number of the attributes of the believers that indicate the loftiness of the values of this religion, and that they walk in obedience to God, avoid His disobedience, and act well in their dealings with His creatures.

[The Commentary]

﴿Ḥā Mīm. ʿAyn Sīn Qāf﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara.

[The Commentary]

﴿Ḥā Mīm. ʿAyn Sīn Qāf﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara.
Just as Allah revealed this Qur'an to you, O Prophet, He revealed the Books and scriptures to the prophets before you. He is the Mighty in His retribution, the Wise in His sayings and His actions.
To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He is the Most High in His essence, His power, and His dominance, the Mighty, to whom belong greatness and majesty.

The heavens are almost torn apart from above them, out of awe of the Most Merciful's greatness and majesty, may He be blessed and exalted. The angels glorify their Lord with His praise and declare Him free of whatever is not fitting for Him, and they ask their Lord to forgive those on the earth who believe in Him. Surely it is Allah who is the Forgiving toward the sins of His believing servants, the Merciful toward them.

Those who take protectors other than Allah, worshipping them and devoting themselves to them: Allah keeps account of their deeds, so that He may recompense them for them on the Day of Resurrection. You, O Messenger, are not a guardian over them to watch over their deeds; you are only a warner. Your duty is only to convey, and the reckoning is upon Us.

And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an, as We revealed to the prophets before you, so that you may warn the people of Makkah (Mecca) and those around them among all mankind, and warn of the Day of Gathering (yawm al-jam'), which is the Day of Resurrection, about whose coming there is no doubt. On that Day people will be in two groups: a group in Paradise, who are those who believed in Allah and followed what His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them; and a group in the blazing Fire, who are those who disbelieved in Allah and opposed what His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them.

If Allah had willed, He would have made all His creation united upon guidance and on one righteous creed, and He would have done so. But He willed to admit into His mercy whomever He wills of His chosen servants. As for the wrongdoers, who wronged themselves by associating partners with Allah, they will have no protector on the Day of Resurrection to manage their affairs, nor any helper to save them from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.

Rather than that, these polytheists have taken protectors besides Allah, who they take as their allies. Allah alone is the true Protector (al-Wali): His servant takes Him as his protector through worship and obedience, and He takes His believing servants under His protection by bringing them out of darkness into light and helping them in all their affairs. He is the One who gives life to the dead at the resurrection, and He is over all things Capable, nothing can overwhelm Him.

And whatever you differ about, O people, concerning any matter of your religion, its judgment is referred back to God in His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). "That is God, my Lord and your Lord; upon Him alone I have relied, and to Him I turn in all my affairs."

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and their originator by His power, His will and His wisdom. ﴿He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and from the cattle He has made for you mates﴾, male and female, multiplying you through this pairing by means of procreation. ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾, and none of His creation resembles Him or is equal to Him, neither in His essence, nor in His names, nor in His attributes, nor in His actions. This is because all His names are most beautiful, His attributes are attributes of perfection and majesty, and His actions, by which He brought into existence the great creatures, are performed without any partner. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾; nothing of the deeds and words of His creatures is hidden from Him, and He will requite them for that.

To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the keys of mercy and provision. He expands the provision of whomever He wills among His servants and restricts it for whomever He wills. Indeed, He, may He be blessed and exalted, has knowledge of everything; nothing concerning the affairs of His creation is hidden from Him.

God has prescribed for you, O people, of the religion which We revealed to you, O Messenger, and which is Islam, that which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus—these five are the Messengers of firm resolve (ulul-'azm) according to the well-known view—saying: Establish the religion through monotheism and obedience to God and worship of Him alone, without associating anyone else with Him, and do not become divided concerning the religion which I have commanded you. Great upon the polytheists is that to which you call them of the Oneness of God and sincerity in worshipping Him. God chooses for monotheism whomever He wills from among His creation, and guides to acting in obedience to Him whoever turns back to Him.

The polytheists did not split into sects and factions in their religions except after knowledge had come to them and the proof had been established against them. What led them to this was nothing but rebellious insolence and obstinacy. Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, O Messenger, to delay the punishment against them until a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection, the matter would have been decided between them by hastening the punishment upon the disbelievers among them. And indeed, those who were given the Torah and the Gospel after these dissenters are in disquieting doubt about the religion and faith, a doubt that causes unease and the blameworthy disagreement.

So to that upright religion which Allah prescribed for the prophets and enjoined upon them, call (people), O Messenger, the servants of Allah, and be steadfast as Allah has commanded you, and do not follow the whims of those who doubt the truth and deviate from the religion. Say: "I believe in all the Books that Allah sent down from heaven upon the prophets, and my Lord has commanded me to be just among you in judgment. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us is the reward of our good deeds, and for you is the recompense of your evil deeds. There is no contention or dispute between us and you after the truth has become manifest. Allah will gather us and you on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge between us with truth concerning that over which we differed, and to Him is the return and the final place, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves."

Those who argue about the religion of God, after it has been accepted by people and they have submitted to it, their argument is void and will fail before their Lord. Upon them is wrath from God in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is severe punishment, which is the Fire.

Allah is the One who sent down the Qur'an and the other revealed Books with truth, and sent down the balance (al-mizan), which is justice, so that He may judge between people with fairness. And what could make you know? Perhaps the Hour, when the Resurrection will take place, is near.

Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten the coming of the Hour, mocking and ridiculing. Those who believe in it are fearful of its occurrence, and they know that it is the truth about which there is no doubt. Verily, those who dispute concerning the establishment of the Hour are in far-off error, distant from the truth.

Allah is Gentle and Kind to His servants. He widens provision for whomever He wills and restricts it for whomever He wills, according to His wisdom, glory be to Him. He is the Strong, to whom all strength belongs, the Mighty in His retribution against those who disobey Him.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 42, verse 20:

Whoever desires by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, We will increase for him in his deed; he fulfils the rights of Allah and spends in calling to the religion. We will multiply for him the reward of a good deed to ten times its like, and beyond that to whatever increase Allah wills. But whoever desires by his deed the worldly life alone, We will give him from it what We have decreed for him, and he will have no share of reward in the Hereafter.

Do these polytheists have partners (in their polytheism and misguidance) who have prescribed for them, in religion and in shirk, what Allah has not permitted? Had it not been for the decree and predestination of Allah to give them respite, and that the punishment not be hastened upon them in this world, the matter would have been decided between them by hastening their punishment. Indeed, for the disbelievers in Allah there is a painful, agonizing punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

You, O Messenger, will see the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection fearful of the punishment of God for the evil deeds they committed in the world, while the punishment is descending upon them, and they will surely taste it without any escape. As for those who believed in God and obeyed Him, they will be in the gardens of Paradise and its palaces and the bliss of the Hereafter; for them is whatever their souls desire with their Lord. That which God has given them of grace and honor is a bounty that cannot be described, and minds cannot reach it.

That is the bliss and honor in the Hereafter that I have told you about, O people, which is the glad tidings that Allah gives to His servants who believed in Him in this world and obeyed Him. Say, O Messenger, to those among your people who are idolaters and who doubt the Hour: "I do not ask you for any reward for what I call you to of the truth that I have brought you, in exchange for your wealth. Rather, [I ask only] that you show affection to me because of my kinship with you, and that you maintain the ties of kinship that are between me and you." And whoever earns a good deed, We will multiply it for him by ten and more. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving of the sins of His servants, Appreciative of their good deeds and their obedience to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 42, verse 24:

Or do these polytheists say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"? But if Allah willed, He would seal your heart, O Messenger, [if you had done that]. Allah eradicates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words, which never change or alter, and by His true promise, which is never broken. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts of His servants; nothing of it is hidden from Him.

It is Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, who accepts repentance from His servants when they turn back to the Oneness of Allah and to His obedience, and who pardons misdeeds. He knows what you do, whether good or evil; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 42, verse 26:

Those who believe in Allah and His Messenger respond to their Lord, accepting what He has called them to and submitting to Him, and He increases them from His bounty with success and multiplied reward. As for the disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger, for them on the Day of Resurrection is a severe, painful, and agonizing punishment.

Had God expanded provision for His servants and made it abundant for them, they would have rebelled in the earth with insolence and arrogance, and some of them would have oppressed others. But God sends down their provision in measure, as He wills, sufficient for them. Indeed, He is All-Aware of His servants, knowing what is good for them, All-Seeing of their management and the disposition of their affairs.

And it is Allah alone who sends down the rain from the sky, so He gives them relief through it after they had despaired of its descent, and He spreads His mercy among His creation, so it reaches them all with the rain. He is the Walī (Protector, Ally), who looks after His servants with His kindness and bounty, the Ḥamīd (Praiseworthy) in His guardianship and His management.

And among His signs, which point to His greatness, power and dominion, is the creation of the heavens and the earth without any prior pattern, and the dispersal within them of various kinds of living creatures. And He is able, whenever He wills, to gather creation after their death for the standing of the Resurrection; nothing is beyond His power.

Whatever calamity befalls you, O people, in your religion or your worldly life, it is because of what your own hands have earned of sins and transgressions. And your Lord pardons many of your misdeeds, so He does not punish you for them.

And you, O people, cannot escape God's power over you, nor can you outrun Him. Besides God, you have no guardian to manage your affairs and bring you benefit, nor any helper to ward off harm from you.

And among His signs, which show His overwhelming power and dominant sovereignty, are the great ships like mountains running upon the sea. If Allah wills, He who caused these ships to run upon the sea will still the wind, and the ships will remain motionless on the back of the sea, not running. Indeed, in the running of these ships and their standing still on the sea by the power of Allah are admonitions and clear proofs of the power of Allah for every one who is patient (ṣabbār) in obeying Allah, in refraining from sins, and in bearing the painful decrees of Allah, and grateful (shakūr) for His blessings and bounties.

If Allah wills, He who caused these ships to run upon the sea will still the wind, and the ships will remain motionless on the back of the sea, not running. Indeed, in the running of these ships and their standing still on the sea by the power of Allah are admonitions and clear proofs of the power of Allah for every one who is patient (ṣabbār) in obeying Allah, in refraining from sins, and in bearing the painful decrees of Allah, and grateful (shakūr) for His blessings and bounties.
Or He destroys the ships by drowning them, because of the sins of their people, and He pardons many sins, so He does not punish for them.

And those who dispute concerning Our signs, which point to Our oneness, with falsehood will know that they have no place of escape and no refuge from the punishment of Allah when He punishes them for their sins and their disbelief in Him.

Whatever you have been given, O people, of wealth, children, or other things, is but a passing enjoyment of the worldly life, which soon vanishes. What is with Allah of the enduring bliss of Paradise is better and more lasting for those who believe in Allah and His messengers, and who put their trust in their Lord.

Those who avoid the major sins that Allah has forbidden, and the gross and repugnant kinds of disobedience, and when they are angered by one who has wronged them, they forgive the offense and pardon the wrongdoer's punishment, seeking the reward and pardon of Allah, the Exalted. And this is among the noble qualities of character.

The commentary on Surah 42, verse 38 (al-Shura):

Those who respond to their Lord when He calls them to His Oneness (tawhid) and obedience to Him, and who establish the prescribed prayer (salah) with its due limits at its appointed times; and whose affairs are conducted by mutual consultation (shura) when they wish to undertake a matter; and who spend from what We have bestowed upon them of wealth in the way of Allah, and who discharge what Allah has made obligatory upon them of rights due to their rightful recipients, such as zakah, support of dependents, and other forms of expenditure.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Tafsir"), on Surah 42, verse 39:

﴿And those who, when wrongful oppression afflicts them, defend themselves,﴾ against whoever transgresses against them, without transgressing beyond what is due. And if they endure patiently, then in the outcome of their patience there is much good.

The recompense for an evil deed is a punishment equal to it, without any excess. Whoever pardons the wrongdoer, abandons punishing him, and reconciles between himself and the one he pardoned, seeking the Face of Allah, then his reward for that pardon is upon Allah. Indeed, Allah does not love the wrongdoers, who begin aggression against people and harm them.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 42, verse 41:**

﴿وَلَمَنِ انتَصَرَ مِن بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُولَٰئِكَ مَا عَلَيْهِم مِّن مُّؤَاخَذَةٍ﴾

Translation of the verse: "And whoever defends himself after he has been wronged, there is no blame upon them."

The blame (the punishment) is only upon those who wrong people, transgressing against them unjustly and aggressively. They exceed the limit that their Lord permitted them, going on to what He did not allow them, so they cause corruption on earth without right. For them, on the Day of Resurrection, there is a painful, agonizing punishment.

And whoever bears patiently with harm and meets wrongdoing with pardon, forgiveness and concealment, indeed that is among the steadfast matters (ʿazāʾim al-umūr) that are praiseworthy, and noble deeds which God has commanded and for which He has prescribed abundant reward and a fine commendation.

Whoever Allah leaves astray from right guidance because of his wrongdoing, he has no protector who can guide him to the path of rectitude. And you will see, O Messenger, the disbelievers in Allah on the Day of Resurrection, when they see the punishment, saying to their Lord: "Is there any way for us to return to the worldly life, so that we may act in obedience to You?" But they will not be granted that.

And you, O Messenger, will see these wrongdoers being presented before the Fire, humbled and abased, looking at the Fire with a sidelong glance, weak and feeble-eyed from fear and humiliation. And those who believed in Allah and His Messenger will say, in Paradise, when they witness what has befallen the disbelievers of loss: "Indeed, the true losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection by entering the Fire." Verily, the wrongdoers – on the Day of Resurrection – are in a lasting punishment that will not cease for them nor pass away.

These unbelievers will have no helpers or supporters on the Day of Resurrection when God punishes them, who could protect them from the punishment of God. And whomever God leaves astray because of his disbelief and wrongdoing, there is no way for him to reach the truth in this world or Paradise in the Hereafter, because the paths of salvation have been closed to him. Guidance and misguidance are in the hand of God, glorified and exalted be He, alone, with none other besides Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 42, verse 47:

Respond to your Lord, O disbelievers, with faith and obedience before there comes a Day of Resurrection that cannot be turned back. You will have no refuge that day to save you from the punishment, and no place to conceal you, and you will have no way to deny [your deeds].

In the verse there is evidence for condemning procrastination, and in it is a command to hasten to every righteous deed that presents itself to the servant, for delay brings calamities and obstacles.

If these polytheists turn away, O Messenger, from believing in God, then We have not sent you as a guardian over their deeds, to hold them accountable for them. Your duty is only to convey the message. And when We let mankind taste mercy from Us, such as wealth, abundance and other things, they rejoice and are glad. But if an affliction befalls them, such as poverty, sickness and other things, because of what their hands have sent forward of acts of disobedience to God, then indeed the human being is ungrateful, counting up calamities and forgetting blessings.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 42, verses 49–50:

To Allah, glorified and exalted, belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He creates what He wills of creation. He grants to whomever He wills of His servants females without males with them, and He grants to whomever He wills males without females with them. He, glorified and exalted, gives to whomever He wills among people both males and females, and He makes whomever He wills barren, so that he has no offspring. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of what He creates, All-Powerful over creating whatever He wills, and nothing He intends to create is beyond His ability.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 42, verses 49–50:

To Allah, glorified and exalted, belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He creates what He wills of creation. He grants to whomever He wills of His servants females without males with them, and He grants to whomever He wills males without females with them. He, glorified and exalted, gives to whomever He wills among people both males and females, and He makes whomever He wills barren, so that he has no offspring. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of what He creates, All-Powerful over creating whatever He wills, and nothing He intends to create is beyond His ability.

It is not befitting for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation (wahy) that Allah inspires into him, or [He speaks to him] from behind a veil, as He, glorified is He, spoke to Musa (peace be upon him), or He sends a messenger, as Jibril (peace be upon him) descends to the one to whom he is sent, and so he conveys by the permission of his Lord, not by mere personal whim, whatever Allah wills to inspire. Indeed He, exalted is He, is High (ʿAliyy) in His essence, His names, His attributes and His actions; He has subdued everything, and all creatures are subservient to Him; He is All-Wise (Hakim) in the governance of the affairs of His creation. In the verse is an affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, exalted is He, in the manner befitting His majesty and the greatness of His dominion.

And just as We revealed to the prophets before you, O Prophet, We have revealed to you a Qur'an by Our command. You did not know before it what the previous scriptures were, nor faith, nor the divine laws, but We made the Qur'an a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants to the straight path. And indeed, O Messenger, you guide and direct, by the permission of Allah, to a straight path, which is Islam, the path of Allah, to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. None shares with Him in that. Unquestionably, to Allah, O people, all your affairs return, good and evil, and He will recompense each person according to his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.
